page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA, and BMI2 instruction sets. A primary characteristic is its resource density: 64 GB of system memory is allocated to just 2 vCPUs, resulting in an allocation of 32 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 322 GB of bundled local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reflect the constrained compute profile coupled with capable single-thread capability. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves strong results, including 2696.08 in stress-ng single-core tests and a Geekbench single-core score of 1580. However, multi-core metrics reveal the bottleneck imposed by the two-thread limit, with Geekbench multi-core (1972) and overall PassMark CPU scores (3136.94) placing in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth achieves 31.81 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 22.36 GB/sec on write operations. Web serving throughput (2.58 GB/sec) and Redis operations (2.04 million SET ops/sec) similarly demonstrate that high memory capacity does not compensate for core-bound bottlenecks in highly parallelized network and database tasks.

The qualitative economic advantage of the E8-2ads_v5 lies in software licensing and memory-intensive architecture optimization. Applications priced on a per-core model gain significant cost efficiency by accessing 64 GB of RAM while licensing only two vCPUs. The integrated 322 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space and cache storage without relying entirely on remote network storage. This profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads with low compute concurrency, such as dedicated in-memory caches, small-scale database engines requiring large buffer pools, and single-stream data ingestion pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance exposes 2 vCPUs across a single physical core, coupled with 64 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 32 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is provided through a bundled 322 GB solid-state drive, while no hardware accelerators are present. Benchmark results reflect this architectural profile: single-core performance remains competitive, achieving 1580 in Geekbench single-core, whereas multi-core benchmarks such as PassMark and Geekbench multi-core score in lower percentiles due to physical core constraints. Memory bandwidth reaches 31.81 GB/sec on uncached reads. This configuration offers strong cost efficiency for memory-heavy software licensed per core, eliminating expenditure on idle compute threads. It is tailored for memory-bound workloads, including relational database caching, small in-memory stores, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
